paragraphs: Dear Mia, Thank you for your email about Snow. Last week, I read a book about the desert in the library. I am happy that you like animals as much as I do. Today I have a quiz for you about two animals of the desert. The prize is a drawing of a camel, and I will send it by email.

A camel is much bigger than a fox. It is taller than a man, and it is heavier than a motorbike. A camel has a hump on its back, and the hump has fat. The camel uses the fat for food. So it can walk for many days without water. When it finds water, it drinks a lot in a few minutes. A camel walks on hot sand in the day. It carries heavy bags for people. Its wide feet do not go deep into the sand.

A fox of the desert is much smaller than a camel. It is smaller than a cat. Its ears are very big for its small head. Big ears keep the fox cooler in the hot sun. Its feet are small, but they are quick on the sand. Its fur is long and warm. The desert is colder at night than in the day. The fox eats insects, small animals, and plants. It sleeps in a hole in the day, and it looks for food at night.

I have a photo of a camel for you. But the photo of the fox is missing. I am sorry, and I will send it tomorrow. My teacher, Ms. Ong, was pleased with my quiz. Now it is your turn. If you know the answers, write back to me. Which animal is bigger, and which animal has the bigger ears? I like the camel more, because it helps people. Tell me about Snow, too. Best wishes, Nadia
text.summary: Nadia, a pen pal, sends Mia an email with a quiz about two desert animals. She compares a camel and a small fox, and she tells Mia that one photo is missing.
